definition: The reactants and products being studied in a reaction; everything outside them, such as the water, container and air, is the surroundings.
A reaction that transfers heat from the surroundings to the system, so the temperature of the surroundings falls and $\Delta H$ is positive.
A reaction that transfers heat from the system to the surroundings, so the temperature of the surroundings rises and $\Delta H$ is negative.
A graph of potential energy against reaction coordinate that shows the levels of the reactants and products and the energy barrier between them.
The heat transferred between a system and its surroundings at constant pressure, $\Delta H$, usually given in $\pu{kJ mol-1}$; negative when heat is given out.
$\Delta H^\ominus$: the enthalpy change for a reaction as written, at $\pu{100 kPa}$ and a stated temperature (usually $\pu{298 K}$), with every substance in its standard state.
The energy needed to raise the temperature of $\pu{1 g}$ of a substance by $\pu{1 K}$, $c$, in $\pu{J g-1 K-1}$; for water it is $\pu{4.18 J g-1 K-1}$, used in $Q = mc\Delta T$.
Measuring the heat released or absorbed by a reaction from the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution; heat loss usually makes the measured value too small.
